title: China Southwest Airlines 4509
summary: Flight 4509, a Tupolev Tu-154M flying Chengdu-Wenzhou, was on approach when the crew extended flaps at 1,000 m; seconds later the nose dropped abruptly and the aircraft disintegrated in mid-air before crashing into high ground near Rui'an and exploding, killing all 61 aboard. The investigation found incorrect self-locking locknuts had been installed in the elevator system without maintenance crews noticing; the nuts worked loose in flight, leaving the elevator uncontrollable and disabling the pitch channel.
probable_cause: Incorrect self-locking locknuts installed in the elevator operating system went unnoticed by maintenance crews and spun off during the flight, leaving the elevator uncontrollable and disabling the pitch channel, causing the crash.

factors.evidence: Incorrect self-locking locknuts had been installed in the elevator operating system, which maintenance crews failed to notice
This disabled the aircraft's pitch channel, causing the crash
the aircraft's nose lowered abruptly, the aircraft disintegrated in mid-air and crashed into an area of high ground, and exploded

events.text: On 24 February 1999 the crew was preparing the aircraft for landing at Wenzhou Airport, and the flaps were extended at 1,000 m.
Seconds after flap extension, the aircraft's nose lowered abruptly, and it disintegrated in mid-air before crashing into high ground and exploding.
Investigators found incorrect self-locking locknuts in the elevator operating system, unnoticed by maintenance crews, had spun off during the flight, disabling the pitch channel.

title: American Airlines 1420

route.to_name: Bill and Hillary Clinton National Airport

location.name: Bill and Hillary Clinton National Airport

summary: Flight 1420 was diverted from its originally assigned runway due to a wind shear alert and wind direction change. The crew requested runway 4R for a headwind during landing, but due to the aircraft's weather radar having a narrow forward-facing field of view and heavy precipitation causing radar attenuation, the crew could not see a severe thunderstorm approaching the airport during their turn. The aircraft touched down on the wet runway, but the pilots failed to arm the automatic spoiler system. Without spoilers deployed, the aircraft could not stop and overran the runway by 800 feet, striking the ILS localizer array and approach light structure.
probable_cause: Runway overrun caused by failure to deploy spoilers on landing, resulting in loss of landing gear effectiveness and inability to stop within runway confines. The aircraft touched down with insufficient deceleration capability and directional control was lost when excessive reverse thrust was applied.

title: Air Fiji 121
summary: Air Fiji Flight 121, an Embraer EMB-110 Bandeirante, departed Nausori for Nadi on July 24, 1999 with 15 passengers and 2 crew. Fifteen minutes after takeoff, the aircraft descended below the Minimum Descent Altitude of 5,400 feet without adequate visual reference. The right wing struck a ridge at 1,300 feet elevation, causing the aircraft to break apart and impact a mountainside near Delailasakau, killing all 17 on board.
probable_cause: Crew descent below Minimum Descent Altitude without visual reference to terrain, combined with the captain's fatigue from insufficient rest and above-therapeutic antihistamine use, and inadequate standard operating procedures.

title: Pakistan Naval Air Arm Atlantique shootdown
summary: A Pakistan Navy Breguet Atlantique maritime patrol aircraft was shot down by an Indian Air Force MiG-21 fighter over the Rann of Kutch border region. An air-to-air missile struck the aircraft's port engine. Sixteen Pakistani personnel were killed. Pakistan claimed the aircraft was on a routine training mission inside Pakistani airspace and did not violate Indian territory, while India alleged the aircraft violated a bilateral 10 km buffer agreement. The incident escalated tensions one month after the Kargil War.
probable_cause: Aircraft shot down by Indian Air Force fighter jet; Pakistan and India disputed the aircraft's location and whether it violated bilateral agreements regarding military aircraft proximity to the border.

factors.evidence: Indian experts questioned why a training mission was being carried out so close to the border, when all air forces conduct training flights in clearly demarcated training areas located well away from international boundaries.
The Indian Air force claimed that the aeroplane did not respond to international protocol and that it acted in a hostile manner.
Pakistan claimed the aircraft was on a routine training mission inside Pakistan air space, while India alleged the plane violated a bilateral agreement regarding 10 km buffer zone from the border.
An infrared homing R-60 air-to-air missile was fired at it by Squadron Leader P.K. Bundela, hitting the engine on the port side of the plane.

events.text: Atlantic-91 left Mehran Naval Base in Pakistan at 9:15 am PKT (9:45 IST).
Indian Air Force ground radar picked up the plane as it approached the India-Pakistan border.
Two IAF MiG-21 interceptor aircraft of No. 45 Squadron from Naliya airbase were scrambled.
Nearly two hours after takeoff from Pakistan, at 11:17 am IST, the Atlantic was intercepted and an infrared homing R-60 air-to-air missile was fired, hitting the engine on the port side of the plane.

notes: Security event; facts disputed between India and Pakistan
Limited technical accident investigation due to political nature of incident

title: LAPA 3142
summary: LAPA Flight 3142, a Boeing 737, crashed during takeoff from Buenos Aires on August 31, 1999. As the aircraft started its takeoff run, the take-off warning system sounded an alarm indicating incorrect configuration. The crew ignored the warning and continued the takeoff with flaps fully retracted. The aircraft overran the runway, breached the perimeter fence, crossed a road hitting a car, and collided with construction equipment before catching fire.
probable_cause: The crew failed to configure the aircraft correctly for takeoff, ignoring the take-off warning system alarm. The pilots did not verify flap position before proceeding with takeoff, and the aircraft was not airworthy according to regulatory requirements at the time of the accident.

title: EgyptAir 990

agencies.name: Egyptian Ministry of Civil Aviation's Civil Aviation Agency

summary: EgyptAir Flight 990, a Boeing 767 flying from Los Angeles to Cairo via New York, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean south of Nantucket on 31 October 1999, killing all 217 aboard. The NTSB concluded the aircraft departed normal cruise flight and dived into the ocean as a result of relief First Officer Gameel Al-Batouti's flight control inputs after he disengaged the autopilot and pushed the elevators nose-down while repeating 'I rely on God,' while Egypt's Civil Aviation Agency maintained the crash was caused by mechanical failure.
probable_cause: The NTSB's probable cause was the aircraft's departure from normal cruise flight and impact with the ocean as a result of relief First Officer Al-Batouti's flight control inputs, for which no specific reason could be determined; Egypt's ECAA independently concluded the crash was caused by mechanical failure.

factors.evidence: The NTSB found that the cause of the accident was the airplane's departure from normal cruise flight and subsequent impact with the Atlantic Ocean 'as a result of the relief first officer's flight control inputs'.
At 1:49:45 he disengaged the autopilot; the autopilot-disengagement warning was not heard on the CVR, indicating that the autopilot was disengaged manually.
Three seconds later, the throttles for both engines were reduced to idle, and both elevators were moved 3 degrees nose down.
The flight data recorder reflected that the elevators moved into a split condition, with the left elevator up and the right elevator down, during the abrupt maneuvers to recover from the dive.
The stress placed on the airframe caused structural integrity to fail at approximately 10,000 feet, with the left engine and other debris separating from the aircraft.

events.text: At 1:48, with the aircraft at its 33,000-foot cruising altitude, Captain El-Habashi left the cockpit for the lavatory, leaving relief First Officer Al-Batouti alone at the controls.
At 1:48:39 relief First Officer Al-Batouti began repeating 'I rely on God' in Egyptian Arabic.
At 1:49:45 the autopilot was disengaged manually, without triggering the disconnect warning on the cockpit voice recorder.
Three seconds after the autopilot disengaged, the throttles for both engines were reduced to idle and both elevators were moved three degrees nose down.

Radar data showed the aircraft entering a steep climb from 16,000 back to 25,000 feet between 1:50:38 and 1:51:15, with the elevators moving into a split condition of left elevator up and right elevator down.
At 1:51:15 the aircraft entered a second steep dive at around 20,000 feet per minute, and structural integrity failed at approximately 10,000 feet before impact with the ocean at 1:52 am.

notes: NTSB and Egypt's ECAA reached different conclusions about the cause; no motive for the relief first officer's actions was established.

title: TAESA 725
summary: TAESA Flight 725, a 29-year-old McDonnell-Douglas DC-9-31, departed Uruapan for Mexico City on November 9, 1999 at 18:59 local time with 13 passengers and 5 crew. Shortly after rotation during the takeoff climbout, the aircraft pitched abnormally high, entered an aerodynamic stall, and nosed over. The aircraft crashed into an avocado field 3.3 miles south of the runway, killing all 18 on board.
probable_cause: Crew failure to use appropriate takeoff checklists prior to departure, pilot confusion about heading during climbout, and spatial disorientation that resulted in abnormal pitch attitude and stall.

title: Si Fly 325
summary: ATR 42 on shuttle flight from Rome to Pristina for UN aid workers struck mountain during approach on November 12, 1999. Investigation revealed crew experiencing fatigue from high roster failed to execute appropriate approach procedure and deviation was not detected. ATC personnel accidentally forgot to track flight during approach and did not pay adequate attention during radar vectoring. Combined with faulty GPWS warning system that company had postponed repairing, aircraft failed to clear terrain and crashed.
probable_cause: Multiple contributing factors: crew fatigue from high flight roster causing procedural deviation; ATC failure to adequately track and vector aircraft; faulty GPWS warning system that company deferred maintenance on; crew descended below minimum altitudes without proper briefing.

title: SATA Air Açores 530M

location.name: Pico da Esperança, São Jorge Island

summary: British Aerospace ATP descended toward Horta in poor weather with heavy rain and turbulence, crew altered flight plan to approach via channel between Pico and São Jorge islands. Aircraft drifted 14 nautical miles off course undetected by crew. Crew lost situational awareness and could not distinguish barometric from radio altimeter readings during descent. GPWS warned 17 seconds before impact but crew recovery attempt was insufficient; left wing struck hillside of Pico da Esperança at 1,067 meters altitude.
probable_cause: Navigation error and loss of situational awareness; crew unable to distinguish altitude indicators in poor weather; deviation from course not detected; inadequate dead reckoning and lack of cross-checking between radio and barometric altimeters.

title: Cubana de Aviación 1216
summary: Cubana de Aviación Flight 1216 operating a McDonnell Douglas DC-10 overran the runway at La Aurora International Airport on 21 December 1999 while landing on a wet runway. The aircraft touched down too far along the wet runway with insufficient deceleration and the crew failed to initiate a go-around, causing the aircraft to run off the runway end down a slope and crash into residential houses, killing 18 people including all three flight crew members and 2 people on the ground.
